sections.sectionPurpose: Capture attention and communicate primary value proposition in under 5 seconds. Establish the customer as the hero and introduce their core desire.

designDecisions.decision: Transformation-focused headline, customer-centric language, max 12 words
designDecisions.rationale: Headlines that promise transformation outperform feature-focused headlines. Short headlines are scannable in the 3-5 second attention window.
designDecisions.uxPrinciple: Hick's Law - single clear message reduces cognitive load and decision time
designDecisions.storybrandAlignment: Opens by identifying what the Character (customer) wants - their transformation
designDecisions.evidenceSource: Building a StoryBrand by Donald Miller, Chapter 2; Nielsen Norman Group headline research
designDecisions.accessibilityNote: H1 tag, minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio, minimum 32px font size

designDecisions.decision: Supporting copy that expands on headline without repeating, max 30 words
designDecisions.rationale: Subheadline provides additional context for users who want more information before taking action.
designDecisions.uxPrinciple: Progressive disclosure - primary message first, details second
designDecisions.storybrandAlignment: Addresses the external problem the customer faces
designDecisions.evidenceSource: Conversion rate optimization research shows supporting copy increases engagement
designDecisions.accessibilityNote: Appropriate heading level (H2 or paragraph), readable contrast

designDecisions.decision: High-contrast brand color, action verb + outcome, prominent size (min 48px height)
designDecisions.rationale: Primary CTAs must be immediately visible and communicate exactly what happens when clicked. Action verbs increase CTR by 30-40%.
designDecisions.uxPrinciple: Von Restorff Effect - distinct elements are remembered; Fitts's Law - large targets are easier to hit
designDecisions.storybrandAlignment: Direct CTA - clear call to action with specific outcome
designDecisions.evidenceSource: ConversionXL button copy research; Baymard Institute form studies
designDecisions.accessibilityNote: Minimum 44x44px touch target, 4.5:1 contrast ratio, visible focus state

designDecisions.decision: Lower-emphasis styling (outline or text), transitional action
designDecisions.rationale: Provides option for users not ready to commit but interested in learning more. Reduces bounce rate from undecided visitors.
designDecisions.uxPrinciple: Commitment and Consistency - small first steps lead to larger commitments
designDecisions.storybrandAlignment: Transitional CTA - nurtures relationship before direct sale
designDecisions.evidenceSource: StoryBrand framework recommends both direct and transitional CTAs
designDecisions.accessibilityNote: Visually distinct from primary but still accessible contrast

layoutRationale.decision: Centered single-column layout with max-width container (1200px)
layoutRationale.rationale: Hero sections benefit from focused, distraction-free layouts. Centered alignment creates symmetry and draws attention to central message.
layoutRationale.uxPrinciple: Hick's Law - fewer visual elements reduce cognitive load; Z-pattern scanning supported
layoutRationale.source: Landing page best practices; eye-tracking studies show centered heroes perform well

spacingRationale.rationale: Generous vertical spacing creates visual breathing room and emphasizes importance. Reduced on smaller screens to maximize content visibility.
spacingRationale.source: modern-design-standards.md spacing standards; industry standard hero padding

colorRationale.decision: Dark/gradient background with light text, brand-color CTA
colorRationale.rationale: High contrast creates visual impact and establishes section importance. Brand-color CTA ensures button prominence.
colorRationale.accessibilityNote: WCAG AA contrast verified for all text elements

animationRationale.decision: Fade-in on load with subtle upward movement, 300ms duration, ease-out timing
animationRationale.rationale: Subtle entrance animation creates polish without distraction. 300ms is perceived as natural and not slow.
animationRationale.uxPrinciple: Aesthetic-Usability Effect - polish increases perceived quality and trust
animationRationale.accessibilityNote: Respects prefers-reduced-motion media query; no essential information conveyed via animation

mobileConsiderations.changes: Full-width CTA, stacked layout, reduced padding, adjusted typography scale
mobileConsiderations.rationale: Mobile users benefit from edge-to-edge buttons (Fitts's Law - screen edges are infinite targets). Stacked layout maintains hierarchy in narrow viewport.

sections.accessibilityNotes: All text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Focus states visible for all interactive elements. Heading hierarchy maintained. No content depends solely on color.

elementorImplementation.notes: Use Elementor's Motion Effects for fade-in animation. Set container to Flex with centered alignment. Use Global Typography for headings. Set responsive padding in container settings.

sections.sectionPurpose: Communicate key benefits and solutions to customer problems. Show how the product/service solves their specific pain points.

designDecisions.decision: Benefit-focused headline that introduces solutions, not feature list
designDecisions.rationale: Customers care about outcomes, not features. Benefits connect emotionally while features inform logically.
designDecisions.uxPrinciple: Focus attention on transformation and value
designDecisions.storybrandAlignment: Guide shows solutions to the customer's problems
designDecisions.evidenceSource: StoryBrand framework; benefit-focused copy consistently outperforms feature-focused

designDecisions.decision: 3-4 cards per row desktop, icon + headline + description format
designDecisions.rationale: 3-4 items is within Miller's Law cognitive limit. Icon provides quick visual recognition, headline states benefit, description provides detail.
designDecisions.uxPrinciple: Miller's Law - 7±2 items in working memory; chunking information aids comprehension
designDecisions.storybrandAlignment: Each card addresses a specific aspect of the customer's problem
designDecisions.evidenceSource: Card-based UI patterns; UX research on information chunking

designDecisions.decision: Consistent icon style, meaningful (not decorative) icons, adequate size
designDecisions.rationale: Icons should aid recognition and scanning, not just decoration. Consistent style maintains visual harmony.
designDecisions.uxPrinciple: Gestalt - similarity principle groups related elements
designDecisions.accessibilityNote: Icons are decorative; text conveys all meaning. Icons have appropriate aria-hidden.

layoutRationale.decision: CSS Grid with 3-4 columns desktop, 2 columns tablet, 1 column mobile
layoutRationale.rationale: Grid provides consistent alignment and spacing. Responsive columns maintain readability at all sizes.
layoutRationale.uxPrinciple: Gestalt principles - alignment and proximity create visual grouping

spacingRationale.rationale: Standard section padding maintains rhythm. Card gap provides clear separation while maintaining grouping.

elementorImplementation.notes: Use Icon Box widget for each feature. Set container to Grid for precise control. Alternatively, use nested Flex containers.

sections.sectionPurpose: Build trust through social proof. Show real results from real customers to reduce anxiety about taking action.

designDecisions.decision: Specific results and outcomes, not generic praise
designDecisions.rationale: Specific testimonials ('47% increase in revenue') are more credible than generic ('great service!'). Specificity demonstrates authenticity.
designDecisions.uxPrinciple: Social Proof - specific evidence is more persuasive
designDecisions.storybrandAlignment: Demonstrates Guide's authority through proven results

designDecisions.decision: Name, role, company, and photo for each testimonial
designDecisions.rationale: Full attribution increases credibility. Photos humanize testimonials and increase trust.
designDecisions.uxPrinciple: Authority and Liking principles - real people are more persuasive
designDecisions.storybrandAlignment: Creates connection through relatable success stories

layoutRationale.decision: Card carousel or grid layout, depending on quantity
layoutRationale.rationale: Carousel saves space when multiple testimonials exist. Grid works for 2-4 testimonials.

elementorImplementation.notes: Use Testimonial Carousel widget for 4+ testimonials. Manual layout with Container for 2-3 testimonials.

sections.sectionPurpose: Drive final conversion by painting the success picture and providing clear next step. This is the culmination of the StoryBrand journey.

designDecisions.decision: Success-focused headline that paints the transformation picture
designDecisions.rationale: Final CTA should show what success looks like, not repeat the problem. Customers should visualize their improved state.
designDecisions.uxPrinciple: Peak-End Rule - end on a positive, memorable note
designDecisions.storybrandAlignment: StoryBrand Element 7: Success - show the transformation

designDecisions.decision: High-contrast, large button with action-oriented text
designDecisions.rationale: Final CTA should be unmissable and clearly communicate the value of clicking.
designDecisions.uxPrinciple: Von Restorff Effect - make the CTA the most prominent element

designDecisions.decision: Brief anxiety-reducer below headline (guarantee, process, what happens next)
designDecisions.rationale: Reduces final-moment hesitation by addressing common concerns.
designDecisions.storybrandAlignment: Addresses failure stakes indirectly by showing the safe path forward

layoutRationale.decision: Centered layout with strong visual emphasis, often with contrasting background
layoutRationale.rationale: CTA sections need to stand out from surrounding content. Center alignment focuses attention.
layoutRationale.source: Landing page best practices; conversion optimization research

elementorImplementation.notes: Use contrasting background color or gradient. Ensure button size and padding are generous.
